sources: Animal Diversity Web (Univ. of Michigan), Mellivora capensis: males may forage as much as 27 km (about 17 miles) per day, females about 10 km; large snakes made up 58% of the diet in the hot-wet season; known to eat a variety of venomous snakes, puff adders among observed prey; mothers move the cub to a new den about every 3 days, carrying it in the mouth; lions and leopards tend to kill only older and weaker honey badgers; https://animaldiversity.org/accounts/Mellivora_capensis/
